provenance.whyThisIsA403AndNotABug: docs/design/empty-ledger-narrowing-ruling.md §E1, UPHELD by Danny on 2026-09-09. transaction-service does not own accounts, so for a caller holding neither `banker` nor `supervisor` the only available evidence of entitlement is the returned rows themselves. The controller computes `ownsEveryRow = accountTransactions.Count > 0 && accountTransactions.All(t => t.UserId == userId)`. The `Count > 0` term means a ZERO-ROW ledger yields no evidence of ownership, so entitlement is UNKNOWN, and unknown errs closed. The alternative — 200 with an empty array — was explicitly REFUSED (§E1.1) because it is a true-looking answer produced by an accident of the query, which is the §B2.2 defect one field over. The seeder was corrected; the service was not.
derivedFrom: src/transaction-service/Controllers/TransactionsController.cs GetAccountTransactions, the §B2.2 authorization block -> Forbid/403 when neither the role permit nor ownsEveryRow holds.

CROSS-CHECK, same capture session: dana IS the owner — GET /api/accounts/e6d8d9da-0395-46f5-bbc6-5c4f74e7f1ce as `dana` returns 200 with userId 0a541523-c58f-4974-959c-2705a6ef948e, and the account appears in dana's own GET /api/accounts list with balance 0. So the 403 is not a mis-scoped token; it is the narrowing, observed.

DISCRIMINATOR, same capture session, same token: GET /api/transactions/account/4b41d623-f40e-4b44-9719-2277eaee17f2 as `dana` — her own NON-EMPTY Checking — returns HTTP 200 with 6 rows, while her EMPTY Savings returns 403. Same caller, same role, same endpoint; the ONLY variable is whether the ledger has rows. This isolates the cause to the `Count > 0` term specifically and rules out the competing explanation that the endpoint denies non-privileged callers wholesale. Without this control the 403 above would be a denial with an ASSUMED cause.
provenance.warning: THIS SAMPLE HAS NO `projected` BLOCK AND MUST NEVER ACQUIRE ONE. There is no successful response to project; the declared projection for list_account_transactions (bind/count/collect) cannot be applied to this object and RAISES, which is the correct outcome and is asserted by src/banker-copilot-service/tests/test_evidence_projection.py. A `projected` block here would be a fabricated evidence row asserting a ledger state that was never read — the exact false-audit-statement the Gate B ruling (§R5) and §B2.1 both refuse. It lives in failed-reads/ rather than beside the success samples because the Gate B consumers (EvidenceContractSeamTests, test_evidence_projection) enumerate the success samples and require every one of them to project cleanly. WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE. It does not prove the status code is stable, and it does not prove the copilot HANDLES the failure correctly — it records only what the service returned. The handling side is banker-customer-read-ruling.md §B3.1's concern and is not held here.
